newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH falls after talks with Miller end.
newsitem.headline: LVMH falls after talks with Miller end.

text.p: Shares in LVMH fell on Wednesday after the group said it would not pursue talks to acquire a 38.75 percent stake in duty free chain DFS from Robert Miller.
Shares in LVMH, which bought the rest of the U.S. company in January, were down 1.35 percent at 1,319 francs at 1520 GMT after the suspension of talks was announced.

They had been up nearly one percent, ahead of the group's 1996 results due on Thursday morning, before the news broke on the suspension of the DFS talks. LVMH had previously said it hoped to arrange a deal with Miller soon to acquire full control.
"When they bought their stake, they said it would increase earnings per share, but that was based on calculations that I suspect were based on 100 percent ownership," a trader said.

He said the market viewed the breakdown in talks as signalling that "Miller's demands are higher than those of the other partners, and the deal will ultimately cost LVMH more money". It has paid $2.6 billion for 61.25 percent.
The trader added that if Miller stayed and did not get along with LVMH, he would make the group's life more difficult.
Miller had been the staunchest opponent of the takeover.
